agent: usage (OpenHOI3: the capital's supply takes booked into the country's usage, as the original books them)
question: Which of a country's goods pools the supply pass's takes out of a capital and a unit's draw in the capital land in, and whether the original keeps any separate figure of them or of industry's use beside usage

struct_fields.name: usage
struct_fields.revises: the comment only: it said what saves and counts the pool, not what writes it - the supply pass's takes out of a capital and a unit's draw in one are in it, which OpenHOI3 had kept apart
struct_fields.comment: a CGoodsPool - saved under the key "usage"; GetDailyExpense counts it. The good is pool + 8 + category * 4. **One pool of everything that left the stockpile to be used** (revised 2026-11-15): zeroed at the head of the day by CCountry::ClearDailyPools, before the supply pass; CSupply::DailySupplyPass adds what a province takes out of a nearer province that is its controller's acting capital (sweep 1), CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel adds what a unit standing in the holder's acting capital is given (fuel only where it burns it), and the production shares add industry's metal, energy and rare materials (FINDINGS-supplypass.md sections 2 to 4; FINDINGS-production.md). The economy ledger page shows it as LEDGER_USED_TROOPS, the top bar's ledger tooltip as RES_USED. Measured: Germany at the 1941.12.11 start, usage supplies 697.444 = Berlin's throughput 689.784 + 7.660 given to units in Berlin.
struct_fields.evidence: Name and type unchanged; the comment gains the writers already read in FINDINGS-supplypass.md (sections 3 and 4) and the measurement. OpenHOI3 booking both takes into its usage reproduces the 1936 start save's usage supplies for Germany (92.666), Britain (75.262) and Ireland (0.300) to the thousandth, and Germany's at 1941.12.11 is our capital throughput + the same 7.660 from units. Shown wrong by a save whose usage supplies is not the capital's throughput plus what units in the capital drew.

struct_fields.name: resources_needed
struct_fields.comment: **What a full day of the country's IC would cost in resources**, not what was used: UpdateIC_IndustryNeed (VA 0x4F13E8) writes TotalIC (+0x604) x 1000 to metal (+0x980), x 2000 to energy (+0x984) and TotalIC x 1000 / 2, truncated toward nought, to rare materials (+0x988), each daily IC calculation; CCountry::UpdateIC zeroes all seven goods first (VA 0x4F0D88..0x4F0DCF) and the constructor (0x4C91F4..) and CCountry_Reset (0x4D390D..) initialise it. The economy ledger's flow page shows it as LEDGER_USED_INDUSTRY (FINDINGS-topscreens.md, page 8), beside LEDGER_USED_TROOPS = usage. Not saved. The name was already used for it in the UpdateIC_IndustryNeed and UpdateIC comments; this is the field record.
struct_fields.evidence: A linear sweep of .text for every memory operand with displacement 0x968..0x98B: the only stores through a CCountry pointer are the constructor's, CCountry_Reset's, UpdateIC's zeroing and UpdateIC_IndustryNeed's three (0x4F13F4, 0x4F1406, 0x4F1462, read by disasm.py: imul by 0x3E8 and 0x7D0, the rare path dividing by 2 with the overflow-checked 64-bit helpers). Every other hit is an esp-relative local or another class (CInGameIdler, CGameSetup). Shown wrong by a store to CCountry +0x970..+0x988 elsewhere, which an indexed store (pool + 8 + category * 4 with a register index) could hide from a displacement scan.
